audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Yone rows 3 and 4-5 and gave Level 6 to Skill, while the whys under those same rows say "Level 3 is skill-decided", "Levels 4-5 are even" and "At 6 you re-take control". The chart and its own explanations disagreed.
audit.why: The packet chart reads Yone, Yone, Skill, Skill, Yone, Yone, Yone — it matches the whys, not the sides. Kassadin hugging tower is a genuine coin-flip at 3-5; level 6 is Yone's because Fate Sealed arrives and Riftwalk rank 1 is still weak.
audit.corrected: Flipped rows 2, 3 (to Skill) and 4 (to Yone) on BOTH layers as one group, and rewrote the three whys under them.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why claimed "Kassadin's ultimate changes the math too" without any number, and dosFull[0].d treated Riftwalk as a cooldown you can wait out.
audit.why: Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2s and costs 40 mana with escalating cost — it is never 'down'. His genuinely punishable cooldown is Force Pulse at 21/20/19/18/17s. Advising the player to engage 'on the Riftwalk cooldown' is advice that never triggers.
audit.corrected: Put the real 5/3.5/2s number on the page, moved the tracking target to Force Pulse (21s at rank 1) and to his mana bar, in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, tradeGood and tradeBad.

audit.whatIsWrong: The range and shield interaction that decides every trade was never stated, and report[5] (Key Ability Interactions) just repeated the Riftwalk line.
audit.why: Spirit Cleave is 700 range on 14s and out-reaches Null Sphere at 650; Null Sphere's shield "absorbs magic damage" only, so Yone's physical Q3 goes straight through it. Null Sphere also "interrupts channels" — Mortal Steel has no channel for it to catch, so it buys Kassadin nothing here.
audit.corrected: Rewrote report[5].t around the 700-vs-650 range gap and the magic-only shield.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing warned about Nether Blade's auto-attack reset.
audit.why: Kassadin's W is an auto reset ("next basic attack deals significant bonus magic damage"), so his burst opens on the attack wind-up, not on a visible ability cast.
audit.corrected: Added the wind-up tell to breakdown.early.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Kassadin must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Full kit online, but a Kassadin who hugs tower and dodges Q3 gives you nothing. Keep the wave near your side so he must step out to farm.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Riftwalk's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: He is scrambling to survive to 6, so deny CS rather than force: Force Pulse is 21s at rank 1 and that is the cooldown worth baiting.

edits.before: Fate Sealed sets up team knockups nothing can dodge. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Kassadin's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Fate Sealed blinks behind the last man and pulls him back in. Riftwalk is only 5s at rank 1, so kill him before that number shrinks.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike at 6. Kill him before it scales. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Kassadin Riftwalk: 5/3.5/2s — far too short to wait out, so punish his mana bar instead of its cooldown. - Force Pulse: 21s at rank 1, his only slow — step in once it is spent. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

edits.before: His mobility spike at 6. Kill him before it scales. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 — you cannot wait it out. Kill him before it scales and stacks.

edits.before: Track Kassadin's Riftwalk: His mobility spike at 6. Kill him before it scales. When it is down — Q3 + E burst, snap back safe.
edits.after: Spirit Cleave is 700 range on 14s and out-reaches his 650 Null Sphere, whose shield absorbs magic only — your Q3 lands straight through it.

edits.before: Q stacking and passive crits win the short trades. Respect Kassadin's Riftwalk completely — the first levels are about banking small advantages, not proving a point.
edits.after: Q stacking and passive crits win the short trades — he cannot answer you in melee before 6. His Nether Blade auto reset is the tell: step back on the wind-up, not on the cast.

edits.after: Stack to Q3, E in once Force Pulse is spent, dump Q3-W-AA, and snap back before Riftwalk repositions him.

notes: The whole page was templated around 'engage on the Riftwalk cooldown', which is unusable advice against a 5/3.5/2s blink — the tracking target has been moved to Force Pulse and his mana. Whether Yone's abandoned body can be attacked while Soul Unbound is active is NOT in Riot's text and I did not assert it anywhere.
